title: Distributed systems
blurb: Consensus, consistency and transactions across many machines, how they fail in production, and how later systems redesigned the classics.

main.title: MIT 6.5840: Distributed Systems
main.why: Papers from MapReduce to PBFT, and labs that build MapReduce, Raft and a sharded key-value store on it. In English.
Logical clocks give a total order in which every process runs the same state machine, until one crash halts them all.

main.title: The Part-Time Parliament
main.why: The original Paxos, disguised as a Greek parliament that keeps one consistent record while legislators come and go.

further.title: Impossibility of Distributed Consensus with One Faulty Process
Paxos vs Raft: Have we reached consensus on distributed consensus?

main.why: Equivalent to Multi-Paxos but split into leader election, log replication and safety, so it is easier to learn and build.

further.title: Vive La Différence: Paxos vs. Viewstamped Replication vs. Zab

main.why: Turning Paxos into Chubby's log took leases, epochs, snapshots, disk-corruption recovery and fault-injection tests.
Coarse-grained locks and small files replicated with Paxos, which GFS and Bigtable use to elect their masters.
A wait-free tree of znodes with watches, on which clients build their own locks, leader election and group membership.
A half-broken switch trapped etcd in leader elections, and the failovers that followed hurt the API for over six hours.
Endpoint lists only need to converge, so LinkedIn moved them off ZooKeeper and cut p99 propagation from 30 s to 5 s.
Failures are the norm, so one master tracks metadata while chunk replicas serve data under a relaxed consistency model.

main.title: Linearizability: A Correctness Condition for Concurrent Objects
main.why: Each operation appears to take effect instantly at some point between its invocation and its response.

main.title: Chain Replication for Supporting High Throughput and Availability
main.why: Writes enter at the head and reads come from the tail, giving strong consistency with high throughput.

main.title: Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services
main.why: Proves Brewer's conjecture that during a network partition a web service cannot be both consistent and available.
Consistent hashing, sloppy quorums and vector clocks keep the store always writeable, with conflicts resolved on read.
Only the redo log crosses the network, to six copies in three zones with a 4-of-6 write quorum, and storage builds the pages.

main.title: Scaling Memcache at Facebook
main.why: Leases, regional pools and invalidations from the MySQL commit log let memcached serve billions of requests per second.
TrueTime exposes clock uncertainty, which lets Spanner run externally consistent transactions across data centers.

main.title: Life beyond Distributed Transactions: an Apostate's Opinion
main.why: Large systems skip distributed transactions, updating one entity at a time and linking entities with idempotent messages.
Two-phase commit across MySQL shards, with an external transaction record deciding each commit.

main.title: The Tail at Scale
main.why: If each of 100 fanned-out servers is slow 1% of the time, 63% of requests are slow; hedged or tied requests cut that tail.

main.title: Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter
main.why: Five layers that each retry three times multiply database load 243x, so retries need jittered backoff and a budget.

main.title: Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance
main.why: Survives replicas that lie as long as fewer than a third are faulty, and its replicated NFS ran only 3% slower.

main.title: Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
main.why: Proof-of-work chains let anonymous nodes agree on one transaction history while honest nodes hold most CPU power.
DynamoDB kept Dynamo's name but little of its design, running each partition as a Multi-Paxos group with a leased leader.

main.title: Diving Deep on S3 Consistency
main.why: S3 made every read after a write strongly consistent, using a cache coherence protocol checked with proofs and model checking.
Hybrid logical clocks and an uncertainty window replace the special clock hardware that Spanner relies on.
EKS replaced etcd's Raft with AWS's internal journal, so etcd replicas scale without a quorum, up to 100,000-node clusters.
